title: Operations Research for Statistics
curriculum_locator: Stat H-205 Operations Research; University of Dhaka four-year B.S. Honours Statistics curriculum, starting session 2023–2024

units.title: Foundations of Operations Research, Linear Programming Formulations & Convex Polyhedral Geometry
scope: Historical evolution, systems methodology, and statistical decision-making frameworks in Operations Research
Mathematical formulation of Linear Programming Problems (LPP): canonical, standard, and matrix forms
Slack, surplus, and unrestricted variables; transformations into standard equality constraints
Convex sets, hyperplanes, half-spaces, convex hulls, and extreme points of convex polyhedra
Fundamental Theorem of Linear Programming: equivalence of extreme points and Basic Feasible Solutions (BFS)

units.title: The Simplex Algorithm, Artificial Variable Architectures & Degeneracy Resolution
scope: Algebraic architecture of the Simplex Method: basis matrices, reduced cost vectors, and optimality criteria
Minimum ratio test for feasibility preservation, unboundedness detection, and alternative optima
Artificial variable formulations: Charnes' Big-M penalty method and Dantzig's Two-Phase Simplex algorithm
Primal degeneracy, stalling, cycling phenomena, lexicographic perturbation, and Bland's anti-cycling rule
Revised Simplex Method in matrix form and computational complexity (Klee-Minty cube vs interior-point methods)

units.title: Duality Theory, Complementary Slackness & Post-Optimality Sensitivity Analysis
scope: Symmetric and asymmetric Primal-Dual linear programming formulations and economic shadow price interpretation
Weak Duality Lemma, Strong Duality Theorem, and Farkas' Lemma of linear inequalities
Complementary Slackness Theorem and primal-dual optimality verification
The Dual Simplex Algorithm for restoring primal feasibility while maintaining dual optimality
Post-optimality sensitivity analysis: perturbations in objective coefficients, right-hand-side resource vectors, and structural column additions

units.title: Transportation, Transshipment & Assignment Optimization Models
scope: Mathematical structure of the Hitchcock-Koopmans Transportation Problem and unimodularity of the constraint matrix
Initial Basic Feasible Solution algorithms: Northwest Corner Rule, Least-Cost Method, and Vogel's Approximation Method (VAM)
MODI (Modified Distribution / u-v dual multiplier) method and Stepping-Stone loop pivoting for optimality
Unbalanced transportation systems, degenerate basic allocations, prohibited routes, and transshipment networks
The Assignment Problem, König-Egerváry theorem, and Kuhn's Hungarian Algorithm

units.title: Network Optimization: Shortest Path, Minimum Spanning Trees, Max-Flow Min-Cut & CPM/PERT
scope: Graph-theoretic foundations of network flow models: directed graphs, incidence matrices, and flow conservation
Shortest-path algorithms: Dijkstra's labeling algorithm for non-negative weights and Bellman-Ford dynamic equations
Minimum Spanning Tree (MST) optimization: Kruskal's greedy algorithm and Prim's cut-optimality algorithm
Maximal Flow networks: Ford-Fulkerson augmenting path algorithm and the Max-Flow Min-Cut Theorem
Project scheduling networks: Critical Path Method (CPM) floats and Probabilistic PERT three-point Beta approximations

units.title: Integer Programming, Branch-and-Bound, Cutting Planes & Dynamic Programming
scope: Pure, mixed, and 0-1 binary Integer Linear Programming (ILP) models; logical constraints and fixed-charge formulations
LP relaxation bounds and failure of naive rounding in discrete combinatorial spaces
Land-Doig-Dakin Branch-and-Bound algorithm: tree enumeration, fathoming criteria, and pruning bounds
Ralph Gomory's fractional cutting-plane algorithm and valid Chvátal-Gomory polyhedral inequalities
Richard Bellman's Principle of Optimality and backward recursive Dynamic Programming (knapsack, stagecoach, and resource allocation)

units.title: Game Theory, Saddle Points, Mixed Strategies & Minimax Linear Programming Equivalence
scope: Two-person zero-sum matrix games, payoff matrices, and rational minimax-maximin decision criteria
Pure strategies, saddle-point equilibrium conditions, and iterative elimination of strictly dominated strategies
Mixed strategies, expected payoff bilinear forms, and John von Neumann's Minimax Theorem
Analytical and graphical solution of 2 x n and m x 2 matrix games via upper and lower envelopes
Equivalence of arbitrary m x n matrix games and primal-dual Linear Programming systems

units.title: Stochastic Operations Research: Markovian Queueing Systems & Probabilistic Inventory Models
scope: Kendall-Lee queueing notation, Poisson arrival processes, exponential service distributions, and Little's Law (L = lambda W)
Continuous-time birth-death Markov balance equations and steady-state performance of M/M/1 and M/M/1/K queues
Multi-server M/M/c queues, Erlang-C delay probability, M/M/c/c Erlang-B loss systems, and Pollaczek-Khinchine M/G/1 formula
Deterministic inventory control: Harris-Wilson Economic Order Quantity (EOQ), finite production lots, and planned shortages
Stochastic single-period Newsvendor model (critical fractile optimality) and continuous-review (Q, r) safety-stock policies
